articles.title: 🚨 Dana White says the heavyweight division isn't waiting around for Tom Aspinall
articles.description: Dana White says Tom Aspinall IS coming back — but only when he’s healthy and medically ready. 👀🔥 The UFC heavyweight champion has been sidelined since suffering a serious eye injury against Ciryl Gane at UFC 321 in October 2025, ultimately requiring multiple surgeries. With speculation growing about Aspinall’s future, Dana shut down talk that he could be leaving the UFC: 🗣️ “He’s not going anywhere. He’s with us, and we’re good with Tom Aspinall.” White says the timeline is straightforward: when Aspinall is healthy and ready, he’ll fight again. Aspinall has also publicly confirmed that he has no intention of leaving the UFC. articles.title: Ian Garry Has a New Target: Michael Morales #ufc
articles.description: Ian Garry has a new target — Michael Morales. After his fight with Islam Makhachev, Garry has looked at the landscape and apparently decided that if he can't get the immediate rematch or another title opportunity, he's going after the next-best option. And Chael Sonnen thinks there may be some serious logic behind it. Garry and Morales have history, including a memorable backstage interaction where Garry kept asking Morales, “Does that make sense?” while Morales politely tried to follow along. Now they're potentially on a collision course. According to Chael, Garry is looking at the entire board and making a calculated move. If Dana White is right that Garry may have difficulty getting another championship opportunity, then the fastest way back to the title picture may be beating the guy who could be next in line. Ian Garry vs. Michael Morales. A win over Morales could change everything. #IanGarry #MichaelMorales #UFC #MMA #IslamMakhachev #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #MMAAnalysis #Welterweight

articles.title: Stop Pretending Gaethje vs. Ilia 2 Is Next
articles.description: Can we stop pretending Justin Gaethje vs. Ilia Topuria 2 is automatically next? Chael believes Gaethje’s next fight could be his last—and Justin has already made one thing clear: if that’s the case, he wants someone new. That’s where Arman Tsarukyan and Mauricio Ruffy come in. If their five-round fight is truly a No. 1 contender matchup, Chael argues the UFC should treat it like one. Let them fight, let a new challenger emerge, and give the winner something meaningful. With Gaethje unlikely to compete again until next year anyway, the timing could line up perfectly. Chael also explains why he doesn’t hate the idea of Topuria-Gaethje 2. Their first fight was far more competitive than the ending suggests. But if Gaethje is really preparing for one final fight, an immediate rematch creates another problem: an Ilia victory leaves them 1-1 with no guarantee the trilogy ever happens. There’s new blood coming at lightweight. There’s a potential No. 1 contender fight already on the calendar. And Gaethje wants a new opponent. Chael thinks the answer may already be sitting right in front of us. articles.title: Alex Pereira Deserves a Rematch?
articles.description: The UFC heavyweight division has two champions, Tom Aspinall’s return remains unclear, Ciryl Gane and Alex Pereira continue to be discussed for an immediate rematch and Josh Hokit is sitting there wondering why he’s the one without a fight. Chael breaks down the increasingly complicated heavyweight picture and why Hokit has a legitimate argument. If Aspinall isn’t available yet, the interim championship needs to mean something. Gane can defend it. Pereira needs an opponent. And Hokit has already publicly called out both men. There’s also conflicting information surrounding Aspinall’s recovery. Eddie Hearn says Tom is back training at full speed, while people around Aspinall have offered very different accounts. Chael explains why Hokit immediately seized on those comments and why the distinction between training and being medically cleared matters. But ultimately, this isn’t about Aspinall’s injury. It’s about keeping the heavyweight division moving. Hokit is healthy. He’s ready. He wants a champion. And right now, the UFC happens to have two of them. articles.title: Pay Attention to Ian Garry!
articles.description: Ian Garry could have come out after his loss with the same message we hear from every fighter: thank the team, thank the fans, mention an injury without really explaining it, promise to come back stronger. Instead, Garry gave us something useful. He called out Michael Morales. Chael explains why that might be a much smarter move than it initially appears. If Islam Makhachev’s next welterweight title defense is already headed toward Carlos Prates, Garry needs another way to move himself toward the front of the line. Morales is undefeated, dangerous, and sitting ahead of him in the division. Beating him would mean something. There’s also Shavkat Rakhmonov waiting to return, Dana White’s lack of interest in another Garry-Islam fight, and the reality that Garry may need to take a much harder road back to a championship opportunity than another contender would. But Garry appears willing to do exactly that. Chael breaks down the chess move behind the Morales callout—and why Garry may have walked away from his last fight realizing something important about himself: he’s better than he thought he was. articles.title: Chimaev’s Next Fight Just Got Interesting #ufc
articles.description: Khamzat Chimaev called out Sean Strickland — but then he pivoted. If Sean isn't next, Chimaev named three potential opponents: Nassourdine Imavov, Caio Borralho, or Dricus Du Plessis. But Chael Sonnen sees some problems. Dricus? They just fought. Imavov? That's an interesting option — but if Chimaev gets Imavov, then who does Sean Strickland fight? And then there's Caio Borralho. Chael is all in. Caio Borralho vs. Khamzat Chimaev is a matchup Chael would watch all day. But more importantly, it could solve Chimaev's biggest problem: proving that Sean Strickland is the only fight left. Because that's what Chael believes Chimaev is really doing. He's not abandoning the Strickland fight. He's saying, if you need me to fight someone first, bring me the opponent. Win that fight, and Chimaev vs. Strickland is no longer a callout. articles.title: Why Wouldn't They Match Paddy Pimblett vs. Ilia Topuria #ufc
articles.description: Paddy Pimblett vs. Ilia Topuria might be the biggest fight the UFC can make at lightweight. A non-title fight that could headline anywhere. Any arena. Any city. Even a return to the Sphere. But Arman Tsarukyan isn't convinced the UFC will make it. His reasoning is simple: Paddy and Ilia are both stars, and when two stars fight, one of them loses. Arman believes the UFC may prefer to keep both fighters winning and build them separately. Chael Sonnen sees the argument differently. Who exactly are you going to give Ilia Topuria that is supposedly “easy”? Max Holloway is one of the greatest fighters of his generation. Ilia finished him. Charles Oliveira is one of the most accomplished fighters in UFC history. Ilia didn't need four minutes. At this point, the idea of protecting Ilia from dangerous opponents doesn't make much sense. According to Chael, they're all dangerous — until they fight Ilia Topuria. So why not make the biggest fight available? Paddy vs. Ilia. #IliaTopuria #PaddyPimblett #UFC #MMA #ArmanTsarukyan #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #Lightweight #TheSphere #MMAAnalysis

articles.title: Arman Thinks He Needs 25 Minutes to Teach Ruffy #ufc
articles.description: Arman Tsarukyan has a unique way of looking at his upcoming five-round fight with Ruffy. According to Arman, Ruffy is a young guy who needs to learn a lesson — and the teacher needs 25 minutes of class, not 15. But when Chael Sonnen asked Ruffy whether five rounds were better or worse for his strategy, the answer was clear. Five rounds are good. Ruffy understands exactly what he's up against. He knows Arman presents a massive physical and mental challenge, but he's prepared for the extra time. And after hearing from both fighters, Chael isn't convinced the five-round format automatically favors Arman. Now comes the bigger question: Will the UFC treat this as a legitimate No. 1 contender fight? Chael hopes so. With the lightweight division constantly shifting and Justin Gaethje potentially waiting for his next opponent, the simplest solution might be to stay out of the way and let these two settle it. No hot potato. No marketing games. Let the winner earn the next shot. #ArmanTsarukyan #UFC #MMA #Lightweight #JustinGaethje #ChaelSonnen #MMAAnalysis #UFCNews #NumberOneContender
